hero.title: No one should have to choose between a safe place to stay and their pet.
hero.intro: Pets provide companionship, comfort and stability during some of life's most challenging times. We bring together organisations from across the UK to improve access to pet-inclusive services and accommodation.

about.intro: KePPT brings together organisations from across the UK to make homelessness services and accommodation more welcoming to people with pets.
history: Pets play an important role in many people's lives, providing companionship, comfort and emotional support. Yet a lack of pet-inclusive accommodation can mean people must choose between housing and their pet.

The IMPACT Facilitator Project: Raising Awareness and Driving Improvements in Pet-Inclusive Homelessness Accommodation aimed to raise awareness and support positive change. It brought together Street Paws, Street Vet, Dogs Trust (Together Through Homelessness), Vets in the Community and Newcastle University.

Although the project has ended, the organisations saw the value of working together to provide a stronger collective voice for change. They chose to continue their partnership as a consortium, with a shared goal of improving access to pet-inclusive services and accommodation.
vision: We are working towards a future where people are not forced to choose between accessing accommodation or services and keeping their pet.
The consortium brings organisations together to share learning, promote good practice, and influence policy to increase the availability of pet-inclusive services and accommodation.

why.pets: For people experiencing homelessness, a pet is often much more than an animal. Pets can provide friendship, comfort, support and a sense of family during difficult times.
why.problem: Across the UK, very few temporary accommodation providers allow pets. Many people have to choose between accessing accommodation and staying with their pet, which can make it harder to get the housing and support they need.
why.quote: Good support isn't just about services — it's about having a life.

goodPractice.intro: Guidance, resources, tools, policies, templates, position statements and examples of good practice.

resources.title: Keeping Pets and People Together Charter
resources.description: The Charter sets out guiding principles and practical commitments to help organisations become more companion animal inclusive. It encourages collaboration across housing, health, local authorities, homelessness services, animal welfare organisations and community partners to create systems that value relationships, promote dignity, and recognise the relationship between a person and their pet as a strength. It was developed through co-design workshops and engagement sessions led by Rosie, IMPACT Facilitator, with consortium members.

newsEvents.title: Promoting Pet-Inclusive Accommodation and Services
newsEvents.description: Hosted by the consortium with IMPACT and Homeless Link, this webinar will explore why pet-inclusive approaches matter, challenge common misconceptions and showcase practical ways organisations can become more welcoming. Attendees will hear from people with lived experience, learn about specialist support, and discover practical steps to become more pet inclusive.
newsEvents.note: Registration details will be shared here.

newsEvents.title: KePPT wins a Paw Prints Award
newsEvents.description: The consortium attended the RSPCA Paw Prints Awards 2026 and won the Prevention and Early Intervention Hero Award. We were also finalists for the Special Award. These achievements reflect the dedication of consortium members and our shared commitment to pet-inclusive services and accommodation.
newsEvents.imageAlt: Consortium members at the RSPCA Paw Prints Awards, with their award.

newsEvents.title: A partnership continuing beyond the project
newsEvents.description: After the IMPACT Facilitator Project ended, the partner organisations chose to keep working together. The consortium shares knowledge and good practice and works to influence policy and practice, helping increase access to pet-inclusive homelessness services and accommodation.

collaboration.impact: IMPACT continues to support the consortium through its National Embedding Team. Marivjena Menka, National Embedding Lead at IMPACT, works closely with members to support the consortium's development, facilitate collaboration, identify opportunities for change, share learning and evidence, and support efforts to influence policy and practice.
collaboration.intro: We welcome collaboration from organisations, professionals, researchers, people with lived experience and anyone who shares our commitment to improving access to pet-inclusive services and accommodation.
collaboration.partners: If you or your organisation is interested in supporting the consortium, sharing expertise, contributing resources, collaborating on projects or helping influence policy and practice, we would love to hear from you.
collaboration.livedExperience: People with lived experience are central to our work. If you would like to share your experiences, story, insights or ideas, we would be pleased to hear from you. Your contribution can help raise awareness, inform good practice and support positive change for people and their pets.
